title: Large potential of performance-based model weighting to improve decadal climate forecast skill
abstract: Decadal climate predictions are sensitive to model initialization and simulation of climate forced response and internal variability. Analogue-based initialization selects initial states matching observations from large climate model ensemble simulations, but neglects model performance. We implement performance-based model weighting, favoring models consistent with observations in climate forced response and stationary dynamics. Focusing on sea-surface temperature decadal predictions, we demonstrate the effectiveness of a deviance statistic, not previously used in model weighting schemes. We conduct performance-weighted predictions of pseudo-observations, targeting model realizations instead of observations, which show large decadal forecast potential skill improvement compared to unweighted predictions. We also find skill gains in decadal hindcasts of 95-year real-world sea-surface temperature observations, however at considerably lower levels. We explain this apparent contradiction by limited intrinsic predictability, similarity between unweighted and weighted ensembles, and inherent skill sampling uncertainties. Our analysis therefore highlights previously unrecognized challenges in validating performance-based model weighting for climate forecasting.
problem: This paper addresses challenges in validating whether performance-based model weighting improves decadal climate forecasts, as skill gains are hindered by limited intrinsic predictability, similarity between weighted and unweighted ensembles, and skill sampling uncertainties from short observational records.
method: We propose a performance-based weighting method to improve decadal climate forecasts by incorporating a deviance statistic penalty into an analogue-based initialization system, favoring the selection of climate models that are more consistent with observations.
task: The task is to assess whether a performance-based model weighting scheme, using a deviance statistic, can improve the skill of decadal sea-surface temperature forecasts.
innovation: This paper introduces a performance-based model weighting scheme using a deviance statistic to improve decadal climate forecasts, demonstrating its potential for significant skill gains while also exposing key challenges in validating such methods with real-world observations.

kg_extraction_triplets.paragraph: In this study, we use sea-surface temperature (SST) time series at the global scale, gridded at 5°º× 5° resolution. As observational reference, we use the ERSSTv6 data set [32], covering the 1850-2024 period. However, we only use ERSSTv6 data over the 1930-2024 period, as there is increasing evidence of a cold bias in SST products prior to this time [33, 34].

We further test the robustness of our results to observational uncertainty by performing the exact same real-world hindcasting procedure but using the 1930-2024 SST data from HadISST [44] instead of ERSSTv6 for selecting analogues and skill evaluation.
